evidence.note: Early grapple play has real payoff structure: after the tie-up the menu offers three 'Grapple control' payoffs and the chosen hip toss lands for 10 ('Hitman snaps off hip toss - Hall takes 10 damage.'), pushing Hall to GROUNDED.
Start of the loop that defines the match: 'The repeated tie-up stalls out - Hall gains escape momentum.' Player momentum falls 5 -> 4 while Hall climbs 1 -> 2.

Eight turns later the identical exchange is still running (tie-up stall on 9, 11, 13, 15, 17, each answered by 'Hall uses the stale tie-up to reset with momentum.'), and both health bars are frozen at 126/116 across turns 9-18.

The match's real climax window is skipped: with Hall GROUNDED at 6 HP the menu leads with two 'Finish' options (pin, plus Sharpshooter at 88%), and the methodical policy takes 'Climb to the top rope' instead. The same window reappears at 87, 95, 105 and 109 and is declined every time.
Hall reaches 1 HP here and never rises above 11 for the remaining 87 turns; subsequent 19-26 damage hits (107, 139) leave him at 1 HP, so offense stops meaning anything and the arc flatlines.
Late match is the same loop as turn 9: collar_elbow accounts for 54 of 88 player turns (move_repetition_rate 0.61), with 26 'repeated tie-up stalls out' lines and 21 'stale tie-up to reset' replies.
Anticlimactic finish after 176 turns: Hall covers once and wins 1-2-3 with 0 near falls all match, while the player never attempted a single Finish.
Menu is honest about the loop risk before it happens: the tie-up note reads 'enter a tie-up to unlock throws and whips; repeat loops lose steam'.

The escalated note is legible and actionable - 'tie-up is going stale - pay it off or reset before they steal momentum' - and the log line names both the cause and the consequence ('Hall gains escape momentum').

Curation is honest at the decisive moment: pin is shown first under intent 'Finish' whenever legal (turns 71, 87, 95, 105, 109), so the 176-turn drag is a player-policy failure, not a hidden-move failure.

Readability gap in the Finish block: pin carries label 'pin' with no number while Sharpshooter shows '88%', so a new player cannot compare the two, and nothing states that the 88% is the chance to APPLY the hold rather than to win.

Groggy is communicated cleanly as a modifier rather than a position: 'Hitman is rattled - when they're forced up, big payoffs may open.' pays off at turn 27 with 'Hitman rises - still groggy from the impact!'
Unexplained rule: a 19-damage missile dropkick on a 1 HP opponent leaves him at 1 HP with no message about a health floor, so the player gets no hint that only a Finish can close the match.
Bare reversal line 'Hall turns the tables!' does not name the move or say what was reversed, unlike the fuller reversal text at turn 20.

stickiness.rematch_reason: The first 90 turns show a genuinely interesting game - grapple payoffs, a top-rope exchange, a blood spot - and the obvious unanswered question is what happens if the Finish windows at turns 71/87/95/105/109 are actually taken. But the last 87 turns are the same tie-up exchange with both wrestlers unable to end it, which is a strong deterrent to queueing this configuration again.
stickiness.next_experiment: Re-run seed 212 with a policy that takes the 'Finish' intent whenever it appears (pin at turn 71 with Hall GROUNDED at 6 HP) and abandons collar_elbow after the first 'tie-up is going stale' note, to see whether the match lands inside the 8-40 turn band and produces near falls.

evidence.note: Discovery moment worth returning for: 'Hitman snaps off flying splash - Hall takes 26 damage.' after a top-rope setup, the largest single hit of the match.
Unexpected content that creates curiosity: 'The crowd gasps - Hall is busted open; blood streams down their face.' - a state event not seen in the other seeds this batch.

Counterweight to rematch intent: by this point the log is 26 repeats of the stall line and 21 repeats of the reset line (log_uniqueness_ratio 0.2653), so the session reads as samey rather than varied.

Big spots do land with state feedback: 'Hitman snaps off missile dropkick - Hall takes 19 damage.' plus 'Hall is rattled - when they're forced up, big payoffs may open.' and a position flip to GROUNDED.
Strongest feedback beat of the batch: 'The crowd gasps - Hall is busted open; blood streams down their face.'

Finisher tagging works: 'Hall snaps off razor's edge - Hitman takes 20 damage.' followed by '- FINISHER - the next cover packs extra heat.', cashed in at 176 as 'The finisher still echoes - +12 on the cover!'
Finish pacing metadata is present and reads well: finish_sequence steps delay 1.0s after 'Referee: 1...' and 1.5s after 'Referee: 2...' before the three count.

Payoffs stop paying off: 'Hitman snaps off diving elbow drop - Hall takes 24 damage.' moves Hall from 1 HP to 1 HP. From turn 89 onward every big spot lands on a health floor, so the biggest hits produce no state shift.
Phrasing repetition dominates the second half - the same two stall/reset lines alternate for dozens of turns, matching log_uniqueness_ratio 0.2653.

top_issues.summary: The loop tax fires but does not break the loop. 'The repeated tie-up stalls out' appears 26 times and 'Hall uses the stale tie-up to reset with momentum' 21 times, yet collar_elbow is still 54 of 88 player turns (turns 9-19, 45-55, 117-133, 143-170). The penalty drains momentum without ever making the repeat unavailable or unattractive enough to stop, so the warning becomes wallpaper.

Hall sits at 1 HP from turn 89 to turn 176 while absorbing 19-26 damage hits (turns 97, 107, 139). Damage cannot close a match, only a Finish can, so an 87-turn dead zone opens whenever the player does not take a Finish window. This is the direct cause of the 176-turn pacing gate failure.

Finish windows are rare and easy to walk past. Pin was legal on only 5 of 88 player turns (71, 87, 95, 105, 109) - all requiring Hall to be GROUNDED - and once declined the match had no other route to a conclusion for the player.

In the Finish block the pin option shows label 'pin' with no probability next to Sharpshooter's '88%', and the 88% is not marked as chance-to-apply rather than chance-to-win. A new player has no basis for choosing between the two match-ending options.
Landing 19-26 damage on a 1 HP opponent (turns 97, 107, 139) produces no message explaining why the opponent survives, leaving the health floor rule invisible.
